questions.q: What should you focus on instead of chasing the next promotion?
a: Personal growth and expanding your skills
Office politics and visibility
Finding a stable, secure role
Comparing yourself with peers
questions.why: Lesson 1 says promotions are largely outside your control, so improving yourself is the wiser investment.

questions.q: What sets a mentor apart from a manager?
a: A mentor is also committed to your growth
A mentor focuses strictly on results
A mentor gives far fewer instructions
A mentor becomes a close personal friend
questions.why: Lesson 2 says both care about results, but mentors add a focus on helping you develop and push your limits.

questions.q: How does the summary describe a typical career path?
a: Bumpy and full of unexpected turns
A smooth climb up the corporate ladder
A straight line from school to retirement
A series of planned lateral moves
questions.why: Lesson 1 warns that careers are unpredictable and rarely progress in a tidy upward line.

A team sport played mainly for fun
A hobby you prefer to watch rather than play

questions.q: How do hobbies outside work help executives, according to the summary?
a: They build an improvement mindset and release pressure
They create useful business contacts
They provide a meaningful second income
They improve physical health alone
questions.why: Lesson 3 says striving sports train leaders to surpass their own limits and let off steam away from the office.
